newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Court okays sale of Marcos jewellery.
newsitem.headline: Court okays sale of Marcos jewellery.

text.p: A Philippine court on Monday authorised the auction of the bulk of a $12 million-jewellery collection of former first lady Imelda Marcos after rejecting a request by the Marcos family to stop the sale.
The family had said the auction would violate a 1993 deal with the government that lets them keep 25 percent of their assets.

The Presidential Commission on Good Government, which is in charge of tracking down Marcos assets, said it was finalising a deal with the Sotheby's auction house of London for the sale of the jewellery, possibly by year-end.
A Marcos aide said the collection included tiaras studded with diamonds, rubies and emeralds, plus bracelets, earrings, necklaces and evening bags adorned with precious gems.
"Some of it were purchased from impoverished European royalty," said the aide, who asked not to be named.

The jewellery, now kept in Central Bank vaults, is in three sets. One set valued at 236 million pesos ($9 million), was seized from a Greek man trying to leave the country after the Marcoses were overthrown in a 1986 popular revolt.
The second set, worth between $2 million and $3 million, was confiscated by U.S. authorities from the Marcoses in Hawaii, where they had fled after the revolt.
The third collection, estimated by the government at 15 million pesos ($500,000), was found in the presidential palace.
The court, in its decision, authorised the sale of the jewellery seized from the Greek national and from the Marcoses.
It deferred a ruling on the gems found at the palace, saying it needed an inventory of the items, and ordered the government not to sell the set.
